issues.body: `route_token = os.environ.get("ALERT_TOKEN") or registry_token` still treats `REGISTRY_ALERT_TOKEN` as the private destination credential. With `ALERT_REPO=private/alerts`, no `ALERT_TOKEN`, and a registry token that can read the destination, `_repo_confirmed_private` probes with the registry token and `_alert_route` returns `("private/alerts", registry_token)`. This violates the documented two-token boundary and can silently lose the best-effort alert when the registry-scoped token cannot write to that private repository. The uninjected default-route test codifies the defect by expecting `("private/alerts", "t0")` while `ALERT_TOKEN` is unset.
issues.fix_hint: Use only `ALERT_TOKEN` as the candidate private-route token. If it is absent, return `(registry_repo, registry_token)` without issuing a visibility probe. Add a distinct-token test with `ALERT_REPO` and `REGISTRY_ALERT_TOKEN` set but `ALERT_TOKEN` absent that asserts registry fallback and zero probe calls; make the uninjected live-probe test set an explicit `ALERT_TOKEN` and assert that token is used for both the probe and the private return.
issues.title: Missing ALERT_TOKEN still selects the private route with the registry token

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 credential-boundary defect remains in `scripts/worker-pr.py`. Although the new fallback assertions correctly require the registry token after a rejected probe, `_alert_route` still defines the candidate private-route token as `ALERT_TOKEN or REGISTRY_ALERT_TOKEN`. Thus, when `ALERT_TOKEN` is absent but the registry token can read the configured private destination, the live probe can approve that destination and the registry-scoped token is returned for a cross-repository private write. The default-route self-test explicitly expects this unsafe result. This is materially the same major finding as round 4, so progress is stagnant.
